spec_match.rationale: Builds the spec's flagship use case — the tabbed carousel — from the real surfaces: scroll-marker-group: before tabs, ::scroll-marker with content: attr(data-label), and :target-current, with the §3.1.9 activation contract explained against the code.

interactive.rationale: The tab strip, snap scrolling, previous/next buttons and the aria-live visible-panel readout all operate for real; markers activate panels by pointer and keyboard.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a labelled tab strip with no ARIA and no switching script; the page's full CSS is shown and contains exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the pre-modes browser generation via the honest partial banner and keeps panels reachable without markers, but does not exercise dynamic slide insertion/removal while the tablist is derived.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5109685301673984, the spec modes section, and the explainer's tabs-mode sample are all linked.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite pins the tabs grammar tiers this page relies on and records the tablist role/pruning contract as manual; the shared support panel on the page shows the per-assertion pass/fail honestly (4 pass / 4 fail / 1 blocked on the Chromium 141 build box).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141: desktop, emulated 360x740 mobile and ?autorun=1 (instant scroll to panel 3) all captured; readout said 'Visible panel: 3 of 4 — Reviews' with the Reviews marker highlighted and console clean. The tabs-mode role/focus semantics themselves cannot run on 141, so that half of the contract is unverified here and the banner says so.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the support probe, the explicit fallback branch, and the autorun scroll landing on the requested panel; an early bug where smooth scroll-behavior made the autorun assert sample mid-animation was found via telemetry design and fixed with behavior:'instant'.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables, marker active state inverts background+color together, buttons keep the global style, and the marker strip has an explicit height so the contain:size group box cannot overlap content.

accessibility.rationale: Scroller has an aria-label, panel changes are announced via an aria-live output, markers get :focus-visible outlines and 44px targets, and the copy directs role verification to the accessibility panel rather than claiming it.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow, no console errors; the tab strip scrolls horizontally inside its own band instead of wrapping over content.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Highlight the currently snapped item in scroll-snapping carousels so state is visible.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The active panel is reflected twice: visually by ::scroll-marker:target-current and textually by the aria-live 'Visible panel: n of 4' readout derived from scroll position.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use :target-current for active-marker styling and keep a text equivalent of the current state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied directly; the aria-live output is the text equivalent.

openQuestions.title: Verify tablist/tab/tabpanel roles and pruning on Chrome 154
openQuestions.detail: On a modes-enabled build, open the page, inspect the accessibility tree for the marker group (should be tablist with tab children and the sections exposed as tabpanels), confirm Tab from the active marker enters the active panel, and confirm inactive panels are pruned. This is the half of the contract Chromium 141 cannot demonstrate.

summary: Product-style tabbed carousel from the raw primitives with the complete CSS shown in-page. Verified headless on Chromium 141 across desktop/mobile/autorun with a clean console; the visible-panel readout and marker highlighting work, while the 154 tabs semantics are honestly deferred to the flag/Canary banner.
